meta.title: @yukino.js/sentry — Frontend Monitoring & Analytics
meta.description: A tiny browser SDK that captures errors, Web Vitals and user journeys the moment your site loads. Three lines to init, zero config to maintain.

hero.subtitle: A tiny browser SDK that captures errors, Web Vitals and user journeys the moment your site loads — three lines to init, zero config to maintain.

showcase.description: A real session from a visitor's browser, streamed to your endpoint as it happens. Errors arrive with full context: identity, breadcrumbs, performance and replay.
showcase.caption: One SDK call streams every event above — no instrumentation in your code.

features.description: Error capture, performance, journey analytics, offline resilience and extension points — all flowing from a single init() call.

errorCapture.title: Full error capture
errorCapture.description: Uncaught exceptions, unhandled rejections, failed XHR/fetch calls and framework errors — enriched with breadcrumbs, identity and the session context around them.

journeyTracking.title: Declarative journey tracking
journeyTracking.description: Page views, clicks and banner exposures via plain data-* attributes. No tracking code in your JSX.

webVitals.title: Web Vitals & timing
webVitals.description: LCP, INP, CLS and resource timing collected on real visits, batched and sent on pagehide.

whiteScreenReplay.title: White-screen detection
whiteScreenReplay.description: Skeleton checks catch blank renders, with a short screen recording attached so you see exactly what the user saw.

offlineResilient.title: Built for bad networks
offlineResilient.description: Events queue locally when offline, batch under weak connections and retry with backoff until your endpoint confirms.

pluginSystem.title: Hooks & plugins
pluginSystem.description: beforeSend / afterSend hooks for PII scrubbing, plus first-class React and Vue adapters and a plugin API for everything else.

features.footnote: All of it ships in one init() call — every module is opt-out via a single flag.

workflow.description: No gateway, no agent, no dashboard to deploy. Point the SDK at any endpoint that accepts JSON.

install.title: Install
install.description: One package, tree-shakeable, with ESM and CJS builds included.

init.title: Initialize
init.description: Hand it a DSN and you're done — errors, vitals and journeys start flowing automatically.

insight.title: Insight
insight.description: Open your endpoint or the bundled dashboard: crashes ranked, journeys replayed, vitals tracked.

install.description: Works with any bundler and any backend — if it can receive a POST, it can receive a report.
install.ctaTitle: Your users already hit the bug.
install.ctaBody: Add the SDK, deploy, and the next crash arrives with everything you need to fix it.

faq.bodyA: Anything else, open an issue on
faq.bodyB: — we usually reply within a day.

data.question: What does the SDK send?
data.answer: Only monitoring events: errors with stack traces and breadcrumbs, page views, declarative clicks and exposures, Web Vitals, and a short screen recording when white-screen is detected. Everything goes to the endpoint you set as your DSN.

size.question: How big is it?
size.answer: The core bundle is a few kilobytes gzipped and fully tree-shakeable — modules you disable in init() never make it into your build.

frameworks.question: Which frameworks are supported?
frameworks.answer: Any vanilla JS app works out of the box. First-class adapters ship for React (error boundary) and Vue (global error handler), and the plugin API covers the rest.

privacy.question: Can I control what leaves the browser?
privacy.answer: Yes. The beforeSend, beforeSendBatch and afterSend hooks let you inspect, redact or drop any payload before it hits the network — and individual captures can be switched off with a single flag.

offline.question: What happens on flaky connections?
offline.answer: Events are cached in localStorage while the network is down and retried with backoff until delivered, so reports survive refreshes, background tabs and subway tunnels.

license.question: Is it open source?
license.answer: MIT. No account, no required SaaS — the SDK talks to your own endpoint, on your own infrastructure.

footer.description: Frontend monitoring for teams who would rather see bugs than hear about them.
